title: Applying Sum & Difference: Simplify and Prove

steps.body: Read backwards, the formulas COMPRESS. Spot the pattern sin A cos B + cos A sin B and rewrite it as the single **sin(A + B)**. This collapses scary expressions: sin 40° cos 10° + cos 40° sin 10° is just **sin 50° ≈ 0.766** — no evaluation of the parts needed.

predict.prompt: sin 40° cos 10° + cos 40° sin 10° — what single value is this?

options.label: sin 50° — it's the expansion of sin(40° + 10°), read backwards

predict.reveal: sin 50°. The four-term string is the sum formula already expanded — recognizing the pattern lets you fold it back to one clean value. On the circle: the folded point and the expanded point are the SAME point, at every angle you can drag to.

widget.prompt: Direct point at θ + 10°. Pick the formula that IS that point in expanded clothing, then land θ on 40° — folding the entry's string into sin 50°.

ghostChoices.label: sin θ cos 10° + cos θ sin 10° (with its cosine partner)
sin θ + sin 10° (and cos θ + cos 10°)
ghostChoices.feedback: Off the circle it goes — coordinates past 1. If this were the expansion, the folded and unfolded forms couldn't name the same point, and compression would be illegal. The cross-terms are what make folding safe.

widget.successFeedback: At 40° the glued pair reads sin 40° cos 10° + cos 40° sin 10° = sin 50° — the compression the entry asks for, witnessed as one point wearing two outfits. Pattern recognition is just knowing which strings are a point in disguise.
widget.lowFeedback: Formula's right — continue to 40°, where the string folds to sin 50°.
widget.highFeedback: Past 40° — ease back to where θ + 10° = 50°.

explanationVariants: cos A cos B + sin A sin B is cos(A − B): cos80°cos20° + sin80°sin20° = cos 60° = 1/2.
The plus between the products signals cosine's DIFFERENCE formula: cos(80° − 20°) = cos 60° = 0.5.

widget.prompt: Evaluate cos 80° cos 20° + sin 80° sin 20°. (As a decimal.)

commonErrors.feedback: 0.866 = cos 30°. The pattern cosAcosB + sinAsinB is cos(A − B) = cos 60° = 0.5.
That looks like cos 20°. The compression gives cos(80° − 20°) = cos 60° = 0.5.

steps.body: A recurring simplification: **sin(x + π) = −sin x** falls right out of the sum formula (sin x cos π + cos x sin π = sin x·(−1) + 0 = −sin x). Every reflection and shift identity from the graphing chapter is really a sum formula in disguise.

explanationVariants: cos(x + π) = cosx cosπ − sinx sinπ = cosx·(−1) − 0 = −cos x.
With cos π = −1 and sin π = 0, the formula gives −cos x.

widget.prompt: Using the sum formula, cos(x + π) simplifies to:

options.label: −cos x
options.feedback: Right — cosx·(−1) − sinx·0 = −cos x, matching the reflection identity.

options.label: cos x
options.feedback: cos π = −1, so the first product is −cos x. The result is negative.

options.label: −sin x
options.feedback: That's sin(x + π). For COSINE: cosx cosπ − sinx sinπ = −cos x.

explanationVariants: The minus between sin·cos and cos·sin is sine's DIFFERENCE: sin(3x − x).

widget.prompt: sin 3x cos x − cos 3x sin x compresses to:

options.label: sin 4x
options.feedback: The minus sign means a DIFFERENCE: 3x − x = 2x, not a sum.

options.label: cos 2x
options.feedback: sin·cos − cos·sin is SINE's difference formula: sin 2x.

explanationVariants: Recognize sine's difference pattern: 70° − 25° = 45°, and sin 45° = √2/2 ≈ 0.7071.

widget.prompt: Evaluate sin 70° cos 25° − cos 70° sin 25° to four decimals.

commonErrors.feedback: 0.6428 = sin 40°. The compression gives sin(70° − 25°) = sin 45° ≈ 0.7071.
0.9659 = sin 75° (a SUM). The minus sign makes it a difference: sin 45° ≈ 0.7071.

takeaways: Recognize sinA cosB ± cosA sinB → sin(A ± B); the cosine patterns likewise.
Shift/reflection identities are sum formulas in disguise.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: the special case A = B — double-angle formulas.

concept.body: Compression: match an expression to sinA cosB ± cosA sinB or cosA cosB ∓ sinA sinB, then write the single combined-angle function.

explanationVariants: The sum pattern gives sin 90°, which is 1.

widget.prompt: Evaluate sin 50° cos 40° + cos 50° sin 40°. (As a decimal.)

commonErrors.feedback: 0.766 = sin 50° alone. The full expression is sin(50° + 40°) = sin 90° = 1.
The pattern compresses to sin 90° = 1, not 0.
